hypothesis: The pinned llama.cpp loader (f74e2fa6a) cannot mmap a pre-repacked KleidiAI weight layout: on-disk repacked types were removed upstream, and every Q8_0 matmul weight is copied out of the mmap and re-packed into the CPU_KLEIDIAI buffer at load. The one format change it supports with the same Q8_0 tensors is less metadata to deserialize. Dropping llama.cpp's text vocabulary (248,320 tokens and 247,587 BPE merges, ~11 MB that llama_model_load_from_file parses into hash maps, and that the engine never uses because it tokenizes in Python) should shorten deserialize/mmap by a fraction of a second and change no output.

conclusion: Small, consistent improvement, no output change. Matched by CPU part (/proc/cpuinfo 'CPU part'; no Graviton generation was observed) and pooled, cold model_load_mmap (deserialize) fell 0.66 s (part 0xd40 8.39 -> 7.72 s, -7.9%; part 0xd4f 7.13 -> 6.53 s), and the cold first request (Init + Duration) fell 0.87 s (part 0xd40 36.03 -> 35.17 s, -2.4%), about 3x the cold run-to-run range of the per-round medians (0.30 s). Restore (-0.02 s) and warm inference (+0.02 s, part 0xd40 +4.5% but -3.5% on part 0xd0c) are unchanged within their run-to-run spread, as expected: the snapshot already holds the loaded model. Peak memory (REPORT Max Memory Used) fell 76-94 MB in every class. 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, 600/600 answers per arm bit-identical to P1's reference. Host variability (host_variability): 200 environments on three CPU parts (0xd40, 0xd4f, 0xd0c), none reporting two; the cold improvement has the same sign on every part and in every round that drew it, and the unmatched comparison (-0.83 s) is smaller than the matched one, so the CPU mix cannot explain it; restore and warm have no consistent sign. No rerun needed; CPU implementer/variant/features, HWCAPs, core count, cgroup limits, kernel and AZ were not recorded and are unknown. The other ~6 s of model_load_mmap is KleidiAI's runtime repack, which no GGUF layout this loader reads can avoid; removing it needs a loader change (a pre-packed tensor type or a cached packed buffer), not a format change, and is out of E5's scope. Weight download is unchanged by design (same path, 0.5% fewer bytes).
